# load student survey
```{r}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)

student <- read_sav(
  "/Users/xutianyu/Downloads/PISA2025/CY09_MS_STU_PUF.sav", 
  encoding = "latin1"
)

```

# extract the variables for this study

```{r}
agency <- student %>%
  select(
    CNT,
    MALE,
    OECD,
    PV1MATH, PV1SCIE,
    ST432Q02DA, ST432Q03DA, ST432Q04DA, ST432Q06DA,
    ST433Q01DA, ST433Q02DA, ST433Q04DA, ST433Q06DA
  )
```

# rename the variables
```{r}
agency <- agency %>%
  rename(
    country = CNT,
    male = MALE,
    math_score = PV1MATH,
    science_score = PV1SCIE,
    
    plan_study    = ST432Q02DA,
    identify_gaps = ST432Q03DA,
    self_question = ST432Q04DA,
    adapt_strategy = ST432Q06DA,
    
    ask_classmates   = ST433Q01DA,
    ask_teachers     = ST433Q02DA,
    ask_general      = ST433Q04DA,
    ask_after_trying = ST433Q06DA
  )
```


```{r}
ncol(agency)
```

# find NA proportion
```{r}

library(tibble)

agency_na_prop <- agency %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), ~ mean(is.na(.x))))

#View(agency_na_prop)
```


# use NA proportion = 0.5 as a threshold, make a table for all the countries
```{r}

high_na_vars_per_country <- agency_na_prop %>%
  mutate(across(-country, ~ .x > 0.5)) %>%     
  mutate(Variables_Over_50pct_NA = rowSums(select(., -country))) %>% 
  select(country, Variables_Over_50pct_NA)           

#View(high_na_vars_per_country)
print(as_tibble(high_na_vars_per_country), n = Inf)
```

# make a table for countries NA proportion > 0.5

```{r}
countries_with_high_na <- high_na_vars_per_country %>%
  filter(Variables_Over_50pct_NA > 0)

print(as_tibble(countries_with_high_na), n = Inf)
```

  select(male, math_score, science_score) %>%

# EDA
## percieved agency for goal setting and help seeking: Lollipop plot
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Calculate country-level mean index for your 8 variables
country_means <- agency1 %>%
  group_by(country) %>% 
  summarise(
    plan_study       = mean(plan_study, na.rm = TRUE),
    identify_gaps    = mean(identify_gaps, na.rm = TRUE),
    self_question    = mean(self_question, na.rm = TRUE),
    adapt_strategy   = mean(adapt_strategy, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_classmates   = mean(ask_classmates, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_teachers     = mean(ask_teachers, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_general      = mean(ask_general, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_after_trying = mean(ask_after_trying, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# 2. Pivot to long format
long_means <- country_means %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -country, 
    names_to = "Variable", 
    values_to = "Mean_Value"
  )

# 3. Find the lowest and highest country for each variable
extremes <- long_means %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  filter(Mean_Value == max(Mean_Value, na.rm = TRUE) | 
         Mean_Value == min(Mean_Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(Type = if_else(Mean_Value == max(Mean_Value, na.rm = TRUE), "Highest", "Lowest"))

# Order variables nicely on the x-axis
var_levels <- c("plan_study", "identify_gaps", "self_question", "adapt_strategy",
                "ask_classmates", "ask_teachers", "ask_general", "ask_after_trying")
long_means$Variable <- factor(long_means$Variable, levels = var_levels)
extremes$Variable <- factor(extremes$Variable, levels = var_levels)

# Define baseline reference (e.g., 0)
baseline_val <- 0

# 4. Create the PISA-style vertical lollipop plot
p <- ggplot() +
  # Light vertical stems for ALL countries (group = country is required for discrete x axes)
  geom_segment(data = long_means, 
               aes(x = Variable, xend = Variable, y = baseline_val, yend = Mean_Value, group = country), 
               color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +
  
  # Highlight lines for the Min and Max extremes
  geom_segment(data = extremes, 
               aes(x = Variable, xend = Variable, y = baseline_val, yend = Mean_Value, group = country), 
               color = "#2b83ba", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # Baseline reference markers at y = 0
  geom_point(data = data.frame(Variable = factor(var_levels, levels = var_levels)), 
             aes(x = Variable, y = baseline_val), 
             color = "#1f78b4", shape = 18, size = 4) +
  
  # Points for extreme countries
  geom_point(data = extremes, 
             aes(x = Variable, y = Mean_Value, color = Type), 
             shape = 15, size = 3) +
  
  # Country text labels next to the extreme points
  geom_text(data = extremes, 
            aes(x = Variable, y = Mean_Value, label = country, color = Type), 
            hjust = -0.15, vjust = 0.5, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Highest" = "#d7191c", "Lowest" = "#2b83ba")) +
  
  # Let ggplot auto-scale with padding so labels don't get cut off on the sides/top
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Self-Regulated Learning & Help-Seeking: Perceived Agency Indices",
    subtitle = "Diamonds represent baseline (0); squares represent lowest and highest countries.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean index",
    color = "Country Extremes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1, face = "bold", size = 9),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

# 5. Save to PNG
ggsave(filename = "~/Downloads/pisa_style_vertical_plot.png", plot = p, width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

## updated lollipop

```{r}
# install.packages("ggh4x")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggh4x) # Required for nested/grouped x-axis labels

# 1. Calculate country-level mean index for your 8 variables
country_means <- agency1 %>%
  group_by(country) %>% 
  summarise(
    plan_study       = mean(plan_study, na.rm = TRUE),
    identify_gaps    = mean(identify_gaps, na.rm = TRUE),
    self_question    = mean(self_question, na.rm = TRUE),
    adapt_strategy   = mean(adapt_strategy, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_classmates   = mean(ask_classmates, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_teachers     = mean(ask_teachers, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_general      = mean(ask_general, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_after_trying = mean(ask_after_trying, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# 2. Pivot to long format
long_means <- country_means %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -country, 
    names_to = "Variable", 
    values_to = "Mean_Value"
  )

# 3. Find the lowest and highest country for each variable
extremes <- long_means %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  filter(Mean_Value == max(Mean_Value, na.rm = TRUE) | 
         Mean_Value == min(Mean_Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(Type = if_else(Mean_Value == max(Mean_Value, na.rm = TRUE), "Highest", "Lowest"))

# Order variables and assign grouping interaction for nested x-axis labels
var_levels <- c("plan_study", "identify_gaps", "self_question", "adapt_strategy",
                "ask_classmates", "ask_teachers", "ask_general", "ask_after_trying")

long_means$Variable <- factor(long_means$Variable, levels = var_levels)
extremes$Variable <- factor(extremes$Variable, levels = var_levels)

# Create a interaction data frame for nested grouping (Goal Setting vs Help Seeking)
# ggh4x looks for interaction terms or structured factor levels like Group_Variable
add_groups <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      Category = if_else(as.character(Variable) %in% c("plan_study", "identify_gaps", "self_question", "adapt_strategy"), 
                         "Goal Setting", "Help Seeking"),
      # Format as interaction so ggh4x nests them cleanly
      Var_Nested = interaction(Category, Variable, sep = "_._")
    )
}

# Apply grouping to our datasets
long_means <- add_groups(long_means)
extremes <- add_groups(extremes)

nested_var_levels <- interaction(
  c(rep("Goal Setting", 4), rep("Help Seeking", 4)),
  var_levels,
  sep = "_._"
)

long_means$Var_Nested <- factor(long_means$Var_Nested, levels = nested_var_levels)
extremes$Var_Nested <- factor(extremes$Var_Nested, levels = nested_var_levels)

# Define baseline reference (e.g., 0)
baseline_val <- 0

# 4. Create the PISA-style vertical lollipop plot with nested x-axis
p <- ggplot() +
  # Light vertical stems for ALL countries
  geom_segment(data = long_means, 
               aes(x = Var_Nested, xend = Var_Nested, y = baseline_val, yend = Mean_Value, group = country), 
               color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +
  
  # Highlight lines for the Min and Max extremes
  geom_segment(data = extremes, 
               aes(x = Var_Nested, xend = Var_Nested, y = baseline_val, yend = Mean_Value, group = country), 
               color = "#2b83ba", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # Baseline reference markers at y = 0
  geom_point(data = data.frame(Var_Nested = factor(nested_var_levels, levels = nested_var_levels)), 
             aes(x = Var_Nested, y = baseline_val), 
             color = "#1f78b4", shape = 18, size = 4) +
  
  # Points for extreme countries
  geom_point(data = extremes, 
             aes(x = Var_Nested, y = Mean_Value, color = Type), 
             shape = 15, size = 3) +
  
  # Country text labels next to the extreme points
  geom_text(data = extremes, 
            aes(x = Var_Nested, y = Mean_Value, label = country, color = Type), 
            hjust = -0.15, vjust = 0.5, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Highest" = "#d7191c", "Lowest" = "#2b83ba")) +
  
  # Use ggh4x to create nested axis labels separating Goal Setting and Help Seeking
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = function(x) sub(".*_\\._", "", x), # Strip prefix for bottom labels
    guide = "axis_nested"
  ) +
  
  # Let ggplot auto-scale with padding
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Self-Regulated Learning & Help-Seeking: Perceived Agency Indices",
    subtitle = "Diamonds represent baseline (0); squares represent lowest and highest countries.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean index",
    color = "Country Extremes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1, face = "bold", size = 8.5),
    ggh4x.axis.nestline = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
    ggh4x.axis.nesttext = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, color = "#1f78b4"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

# 5. Save to PNG
ggsave(filename = "~/Downloads/pisa_style_vertical_plot.png", plot = p, width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```










## Help seeking: Diverging Stacked Bar Charts

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Select the help-seeking variables
help_vars <- c("ask_classmates", "ask_teachers", "ask_general", "ask_after_trying")

# 2. Reshape and calculate overall proportions for each category
overall_props <- agency1 %>%
  select(all_of(help_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Response") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Response)) %>%
  count(Variable, Response) %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  mutate(
    Prop = n / sum(n),
    Percentage = Prop * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Response = factor(Response))

# 3. Create a single combined Diverging Stacked Bar Chart
p <- ggplot(overall_props, aes(x = Variable, y = Prop, fill = Response)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.6) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "RdBu", name = "Response\nCategory") +
  labs(
    title = "Overall Distribution of Help-Seeking Likert Responses",
    subtitle = "Aggregated across all respondents in the dataset",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Proportion"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

# 4. Save the plot to PNG
ggsave(filename = "~/Downloads/overall_help_seeking_bars.png", plot = p, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

## scatterplot of math and science score

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel) # Recommended for non-overlapping country labels

# 1. Calculate country-level mean scores for math and science
country_scores <- agency1 %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    math_score    = mean(math_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    science_score = mean(science_score, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(math_score) & !is.na(science_score))

# 2. Create the scatterplot with country labels
p <- ggplot(country_scores, aes(x = math_score, y = science_score, label = country)) +
  geom_point(color = "#1f78b4", size = 2.5, shape = 18) +
  # Use geom_text_repel so country labels don't overlap with each other
  geom_text_repel(size = 3, box.padding = 0.3, point.padding = 0.3, max.overlaps = Inf) +
  labs(
    title = "Country-Level Mean Performance in Math and Science",
    x = "Mean Math Score",
    y = "Mean Science Score"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  )

# Print plot to console
print(p)

# 3. Save the plot to PNG
ggsave(filename = "~/Downloads/country_math_science_scatter.png", plot = p, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

# HCA heatmaps: uncentered correlation + average linkage


```{r}

  install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("hopach", update = FALSE, ask = FALSE)
```


```{r}

# choose variables to create the heatmap
selected_vars <- c("plan_study", "identify_gaps", "self_question", "adapt_strategy", 
                   "ask_classmates", "ask_teachers", "ask_general", "ask_after_trying")

country_data <- agency1 %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    across(all_of(selected_vars), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    # male = mean(male, na.rm = TRUE),           
    math_score = mean(math_score, na.rm = TRUE),     
    science_score = mean(science_score, na.rm = TRUE)      
  )

# change into full country names
country_names_map <- c(
  "AUT" = "Austria", "CHE" = "Switzerland", "GRC" = "Greece", "LTU" = "Lithuania",
  "BGR" = "Bulgaria", "LVA" = "Latvia", "DEU" = "Germany", "ITA" = "Italy",

  "KAZ" = "Kazakhstan", "KEN" = "Kenya", "KSV" = "Kosovo", "MAR" = "Morocco",
  "PSE" = "Palestine", "ESP" = "Spain", "CHL" = "Chile", "CAN" = "Canada",
  "SWE" = "Sweden", "ARG" = "Argentina", "PRT" = "Portugal", "PRY" = "Paraguay",
  "MNG" = "Mongolia", "CRI" = "Costa Rica", "MYS" = "Malaysia", "BRN" = "Brunei",
  "SGP" = "Singapore", "MEX" = "Mexico", "GTM" = "Guatemala", "COL" = "Colombia",
  "ECU" = "Ecuador", "ISL" = "Iceland", "USA" = "United States"
)

country_data$Country_Name <- unname(country_names_map[country_data$country])
country_data$Country_Name[is.na(country_data$Country_Name)] <- country_data$country[is.na(country_data$Country_Name)]

# scale the dataset
data_matrix <- as.matrix(country_data %>% select(all_of(selected_vars)))
rownames(data_matrix) <- country_data$Country_Name
data.scale.subset <- scale(data_matrix)

# distance measures
uncenter.dist <- function(m) {
  as.dist(as.matrix(hopach::distancematrix(m, d = "cosangle")))
}

row.clus <- tryCatch({
  hclust(uncenter.dist(data.scale.subset), method = "ave")
}, error = function(e) {
  hclust(dist(data.scale.subset), method = "ave")
})

col.clus <- tryCatch({
  hclust(uncenter.dist(t(data.scale.subset)), method = "ave")
}, error = function(e) {
  hclust(dist(t(data.scale.subset)), method = "ave")
})

# rightside annotation
right_anno <- rowAnnotation(
  # Male_Prop = country_data$male,
  Math = country_data$math_score,
  Science = country_data$science_score,
  col = list(
    #Male_Prop = colorRamp2(c(min(country_data$male, na.rm = TRUE), 
                            # mean(country_data$male, na.rm = TRUE),
                            # max(country_data$male, na.rm = TRUE)), 
                          #  c("#ffffcc", "#ffbb78", "#d95f0e")),
    Math = colorRamp2(c(min(country_data$math_score, na.rm = TRUE), 
                        mean(country_data$math_score, na.rm = TRUE), 
                        max(country_data$math_score, na.rm = TRUE)), 
                      c("#edf8e5", "#a1d99b", "#238b45")),
    Science = colorRamp2(c(min(country_data$science_score, na.rm = TRUE), 
                           mean(country_data$science_score, na.rm = TRUE), 
                           max(country_data$science_score, na.rm = TRUE)), 
                         c("#f7fbff", "#a6bddb", "#2b8cbe"))
  ),
  simple_anno_size = unit(0.35, "cm"),
  annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8)
)


png("~/Downloads/agency_heatmap.png", width = 12, height = 12, units = "in", res = 300)
Heatmap(
  data.scale.subset, 
  name = "agency heatmap", 
  cluster_rows = row.clus,        
  cluster_columns = col.clus,     
  row_split = 4,
  column_split = 2,
  top_annotation = HeatmapAnnotation(
    foo = anno_block(
      gp = gpar(fill = c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8")),
      labels = c("Goal Setting", "Help Seeking"), 
      labels_gp = gpar(col = "white", fontsize = 10)
    )
  ),
  left_annotation = rowAnnotation(
    foo = anno_block(
      gp = gpar(fill = 2:5),
      labels = c("Low Goal / High Help", "Low Goal / Low Help", "Moderate Goal / Moderate Help", "High Goal / Low Help"), 
      labels_gp = gpar(col = "white", fontsize = 8)
    )
  ),
  right_annotation = right_anno,
  show_row_names = TRUE,          
  row_names_side = "right",       
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 7),     
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 9),  
  column_title = "Hierarchical Clustering Analysis of perceived agency PISA 2025",
  column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold")
)
```
